title.en: What I still do not know

can_do: I can choose among every structure English has, according to the occasion.
I can work out an unfamiliar form rather than treating it as a mistake.
I can say what I still do not know.

ex: A fickle audience that loved the first book and ignored the second.
The weather there is fickle in April and settled by June.
Attention flagged in the second hour and the chair called a break.
Sales flagged over the summer and recovered in September.
A fraught meeting that ended better than it began.
The whole question is fraught with history nobody wants to open.
An impetuous resignation that he withdrew within a week.
Impetuous at twenty-five and extremely careful at fifty.
An itinerant teacher who covered nine villages by bicycle.
Itinerant labour built the line and left no record of itself.
He was nonplussed by a question nobody had thought to ask.
Nonplussed for a second, she answered it perfectly.
A parochial debate about a problem that is the same in forty countries.
Parochial concerns are still concerns and they decide elections.
A peripatetic career across four institutions and two languages.
The peripatetic music teacher comes on Tuesdays.
A pragmatic compromise that nobody defends and everybody uses.
Pragmatic about the method and uncompromising about the evidence.
A precocious reader who found the library before the playground.
Precocious at twelve and perfectly ordinary at thirty, which is fine.
A penchant for footnotes that his readers have learned to enjoy.
She has a penchant for buildings nobody else wants.
A quixotic attempt to reopen a line closed in 1964.
The quixotic part of the plan turned out to be the part that worked.
The committee vacillated for three months and the offer expired.
He vacillated in public and had decided before the meeting began.
A vacuous statement that took four people a day to draft.
The question was not vacuous; the answer was.
They wrested the concession from a ministry that had refused twice.
Wresting a clear sentence out of that paragraph took an afternoon.
The inexorable arithmetic of an ageing population.
Slow, inexorable and perfectly predictable for twenty years.
A bucolic scene on the label and a factory behind the photographer.
Bucolic in summer; in February it is forty minutes from a shop.
Six skeins of undyed wool and a pattern from her grandmother.
A skein of obligations that no single contract explains.
They walked back in the gloaming without saying much.
In the gloaming the whole valley turns one colour.
A rivulet crosses the path and disappears under the road.
Rivulets of rain ran down the inside of the window.
Deep loam along the river and stony ground fifty metres up.
The loam here will grow anything and holds water badly.

p.text: Which gaps does Aziz name in his own English?
options: Formal letters, and the names of the forms
Reading aloud, and hearing his own voice
Jokes land late; warmth is hard to judge
Long sentences, and the use of the colon

fb.correct: 'I hear a joke half a second after the room does.'
fb.incorrect_default: 'I hear a joke half a second after the room does.'

p.text: How does Sarah describe fluency at the end?
options: Writing a letter that needs no repair
Reading a page without meeting a gap
Knowing what you are choosing between
Never having to stop and think again

fb.correct: 'Now you know what you are choosing between. That is all fluency ever was.'
fb.incorrect_default: 'Now you know what you are choosing between. That is all fluency ever was.'

1.say: You have a choice on every line now, and you cannot tell me how you make it. I can tell you afterwards. Not while I am making it. That is what it is to have the whole system. You stopped naming the rules about a year ago. I still stop. Yesterday I could not decide between a colon and a full stop for an hour. What did you choose? The full stop. I still do not know whether it was right. You never will, and that is not a gap in your English. There are gaps. I hear a joke half a second after the room does. I cannot tell which of two words is the warmer one without asking somebody. Nor can I in Uzbek, and I have been reading it for six years. Kamola says it takes another lifetime. It takes a lifetime and then it is not finished. You will meet a word at sixty that you were certain of at thirty. When I came to this office I could not write a letter asking for a form. You wrote one. It was four lines, every one of them was wrong, and you sent it anyway. That was the important part. And now? Now you know what you are choosing between. That is all fluency ever was.

explanation.uz: C2 — ona tili darajasi emas va bo'lishi ham kerak emas. C2 so'zlovchi hali ham bir viloyat iborasini, bir kasbning uslubini uchratadi. O'zgargan narsa — javob: vahima emas, ishonchli usul.

story.title: What I still do not know

body.speaker: Sarah
body.text: You have a choice on every line now, and you cannot tell me how you make it.

body.speaker: Aziz
body.text: I can tell you afterwards. Not while I am making it.

body.speaker: Sarah
body.text: That is what it is to have the whole system. You stopped naming the rules about a year ago.

body.speaker: Aziz
body.text: I still stop. Yesterday I could not decide between a colon and a full stop for an hour.

body.speaker: Aziz
body.text: The full stop. I still do not know whether it was right.

body.speaker: Sarah
body.text: You never will, and that is not a gap in your English.

body.speaker: Aziz
body.text: There are gaps. I hear a joke half a second after the room does. I cannot tell which of two words is the warmer one without asking somebody.

body.speaker: Sarah
body.text: Nor can I in Uzbek, and I have been reading it for six years.

body.speaker: Aziz
body.text: Kamola says it takes another lifetime.

body.speaker: Sarah
body.text: It takes a lifetime and then it is not finished. You will meet a word at sixty that you were certain of at thirty.

body.speaker: Aziz
body.text: When I came to this office I could not write a letter asking for a form.

body.speaker: Sarah
body.text: You wrote one. It was four lines, every one of them was wrong, and you sent it anyway. That was the important part.

body.speaker: Sarah
body.text: Now you know what you are choosing between. That is all fluency ever was.
